source.title: The Curious Case of Convex Neural Networks
source.authors: S. Sivaprasad; Ankur Singh; Naresh Manwani; Vineet Gandhi

record.tranche_reason: The paper directly compares convex-constrained and unconstrained networks on training and test performance, including randomized labels; it argues that restricting capacity can reduce overfitting and resist memorization.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper's own train/test comparisons, randomized-label results, and duplicate-free dataset comparison. Cited prior results are not rows. Calibration and ensemble results are omitted because they do not measure the mapped claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces memorization and natural-label generalization in AllConv and MLP, bearing on V1 in additional architectures. Its own convolutional-versus-fully-connected accuracy comparisons also test V3. Convex constraints preventing memorization do not refute V1's coexistence finding.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: IOC constraints reduce train–test gaps, resist label noise, improve MLP accuracy on five of six datasets, and retain what the authors call comparable convolutional accuracy. Qualify that characterization: the single-model IOC convolutional accuracies are consistently lower, and smaller gaps partly accompany substantially lower training accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces convexity constraints, ELU in place of ReLU, input whitening, more nodes in the first layer, exponentiated constrained weights, and a slower learning-rate decay schedule; comparisons use Adam and early stopping for the baseline experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports results varying dataset, architecture, label-noise percentage, and evaluation at peak versus convergence. It also reports that IOC modifications include whitening, first-layer width increases, activation changes, and slower learning-rate decay.

fits_no_version.finding: IOC-AllConv remains near chance on both training and test sets with fully randomized labels, despite strong natural-label classification performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-output convex constraints can prevent random-label memorization while preserving useful natural-label classification.

fits_no_version.finding: IOC constraints reduce train–test gaps, improve MLP test accuracy, and reduce single-model convolutional test accuracy in the reported comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convex constraints reduce fitting capacity and train–test gaps, with architecture-dependent effects on held-out accuracy.

record.problems: The random-label comparison is reported for AllConv and IOC-AllConv; the corresponding natural-label comparison uses true-label AllConv and IOC-AllConv. Thus it does not show that the same standard unconstrained recipe both fits random labels and generalizes on natural labels. The IOC counterparts change activation, constraints, whitening, first-layer size, and learning-rate schedule. Some reported training accuracies for IOC models are substantially below those of base models. Table values do not provide uncertainty except for repeated CIFAR-10 results in Appendix C.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for intermediate random-label percentages and peak checkpoints in Table 3 are omitted; the 100% randomized-label convergence comparison is retained. Table 1/2 duplicated architecture results are not entered twice. Figure-only training curves and calibration diagrams are not extracted as claim rows.

untested.parts: The original architectures and ImageNet setting are not reproduced. The study uses Adam, batch normalization, augmentation in convolutional comparisons, and early stopping for baseline experiments; it does not isolate coexistence without explicit regularization or establish identical stopping budgets across label conditions.
No width sweep through and beyond interpolation.

No isolation of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, or initialization of a fully connected network from a trained convolutional network. Architecture-specific recipes prevent attributing the entire accuracy difference to connectivity.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization measures.
No influence-based selection and removal of memorized training examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: The study's MLP random-label result: 100% training accuracy and approximately 10% test accuracy. The IOC-MLP comparator remains near 10% on both sets. The prose identifies MLP despite inconsistent AllConv wording in the figure's overall caption.
missing.locator: Introduction, discussion of Figure 1(b), and Figure 1 caption

missing.what: CIFAR-10 DenseNet and IOC-DenseNet test accuracies, 94.06% and 91.12%, which complete the convolutional-versus-MLP comparison.

CIFAIR-10 convolutional test accuracies: AllConv 91.14%, DenseNet 93.28%, IOC-AllConv 90.47%, IOC-DenseNet 90.73%. Table 5's unconstrained AllConv drop of 0.66 is inconsistent with its printed endpoints, which imply 1.66 points.
Five-run CIFAR-10 results with reported confidence intervals: MLP 63.83±0.12%, AllConv 92.21±0.18%, DenseNet 93.86±0.46%; IOC counterparts 69.89±0.21%, 90.34±0.20%, and 90.43±0.59%.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. IOC resistance to memorization does not qualify or contradict the existential coexistence claim in V1. The natural-label architecture comparisons independently support V3, which the record overlooked.

versions.untested_parts: The same architectures and recipes are not compared on both fixed random and natural labels across all stated models; the randomized-label study uses AllConv and IOC-AllConv, with no Inception, AlexNet, or MLP random-label result in Table 3.

relation.reason: Its own natural-label and random-label experiments test V1, and its convolutional-versus-MLP accuracy comparisons test V3.

tranche.reason: The study reports V1 coexistence results in additional architectures and V3 comparisons in unconstrained and input-output-convex settings. Failure of constrained networks to memorize does not contradict V1.

source_check.notes: The MLP random-label experiment supporting l1 lacks a listed row. Source discrepancies are preserved correctly: CIFAR-10 MLP training accuracy differs between Tables 1 and 2, and Table 2 prints a 1.9-point IOC-AllConv CIFAR-100 gap while the prose and subtraction give 1.99.

reader_labels.reason: AllConv has near-complete training fit and 10.1 test accuracy on randomized labels (R3), while IOC-AllConv does not fit the randomized labels (R4); on true labels, IOC-AllConv has above-chance test accuracy (R2).
